marking.note: 1 mark per correct answer, no negative marking.

questions.stem: Enterochromaffin-like cells of stomach secrete:
questions.explanation: Enterochromaffin-like cells secrete histamine.

questions.stem: Lingual lipase plays a role in the digestion of fats and is secreted by _____:
questions.explanation: Lingual lipase is secreted by Ebner's glands of the tongue.

questions.stem: The site of B12 absorption in intestine is:
questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 is absorbed in the ileum.

questions.stem: Face of Golgi bodies towards the nucleus is called:
questions.explanation: The cis-face of the Golgi faces the nucleus.

questions.stem: Most cells of alveolar walls are:
questions.explanation: Squamous (type I) cells line most of the alveolar walls.

questions.stem: The base plate of bacteriophage is made of:
questions.explanation: The base plate of a bacteriophage is made of protein.

questions.stem: Which one of the following represents a saturated fatty acid?
questions.explanation: Palmitic and stearic acids are both saturated fatty acids.

questions.stem: The most abundant biomolecules on the earth is:
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are the most abundant biomolecules on Earth.

questions.stem: In chlorophyll molecules, the functional group is attached to 2nd pyrrole at carbon no:
questions.explanation: The functional group attaches to the 2nd pyrrole at carbon 3.

questions.stem: Myoglobin combines with:
questions.explanation: Myoglobin binds a single oxygen molecule.

questions.stem: Which one is not found in fatty acid of acylglycerol?
questions.explanation: Fatty acids of acylglycerols normally have even carbon chains; C-25 is not found.

questions.stem: Who proved that O2 comes from water and not from CO2 in photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Van Niel proved that O2 comes from water in photosynthesis.

questions.stem: Which of the following stages of swallowing is voluntary?
questions.explanation: The oral stage of swallowing is voluntary.

questions.stem: HIV destroys which of the following immune cells?
questions.explanation: HIV destroys helper T-cells.

questions.stem: Which part of enzyme is denatured by heat?
questions.explanation: The apoenzyme (protein part) is denatured by heat.

questions.stem: Defects in CFTR gene cause _____ disease:
questions.explanation: CFTR defects cause cystic fibrosis.

questions.stem: Each molecule of NADH entering in electron transport chain produces:
questions.explanation: Each NADH in the ETC produces 3 ATP.

questions.stem: Intrinsic factor in stomach is secreted by:
questions.explanation: Intrinsic factor is secreted by the parietal cells.

questions.stem: Teeth adapted for cutting are:
questions.explanation: Incisors are adapted for cutting.

questions.stem: Bone forming cells are known as:
questions.explanation: Osteoblasts are the bone-forming cells.

questions.stem: Phospholipid with unsaturated fatty acid tail makes membranes:
questions.explanation: Unsaturated tails make membranes more fluid.

questions.stem: Micro villi are also called:
questions.explanation: Microvilli are also called villi (of the brush border).

questions.stem: The genes for all of the following characters are linked except:
questions.explanation: Phenylketonuria is not part of the same linkage group.

questions.stem: Syphilis is caused by a spirochete called:
questions.explanation: Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum.

questions.stem: Total NADH2 formed by one glucose molecule during Krebs cycle are:
questions.explanation: Krebs cycle yields 6 NADH2 per glucose.

questions.stem: Churning action of stomach helps in ______ digestion.
questions.explanation: Churning is mechanical digestion.

questions.stem: The cartilage present in trachea is:
questions.explanation: Tracheal rings are hyaline cartilage.

questions.stem: Artificial heart pacemaker is implanted near the:
questions.explanation: Artificial pacemakers are placed near the SA node.

questions.stem: All are the functions of antibody except:
questions.explanation: Chemotaxis is not a function of antibodies.

questions.stem: All of the following are properties of water except:
questions.explanation: Water has maximum density at 4 C, not 0 C.

questions.stem: Which one of the following has thick fibers and more cytoplasm?
questions.explanation: Dendrites have thick fibres and more cytoplasm.

questions.stem: Mandible is the bone of _______.
questions.explanation: The mandible is the lower jaw bone.

questions.stem: The lymph capillary of small intestine is:
questions.explanation: The lymph capillary of the small intestine is the lacteal.

questions.stem: If father of a baby is normal and mother is haemophilic then chances of the male baby in inheriting the
questions.explanation: All sons inherit Xh from the haemophilic mother, so 100% are affected.

questions.stem: Salient feature of Darwin-Wallace theory is:
questions.explanation: Variation, natural selection and speciation are all salient features.

questions.stem: All or None phenomenon is seen in:
questions.explanation: All-or-none phenomenon is seen in a single muscle fibre.

questions.stem: The primary nitrogenous waste is:
questions.explanation: Ammonia is the primary nitrogenous waste.

questions.stem: The inhibitors which make strong covalent bond with active site is called:
questions.explanation: Inhibitors forming a strong covalent bond are irreversible.

questions.stem: The cellular immune response occurs in ______ phase:
questions.explanation: Cellular immune response occurs in activation and effector phases.

questions.stem: The mammalian enzymes are more active at temperature of:
questions.explanation: Mammalian enzymes are most active near 40 C.

questions.stem: The portion of the circulatory bed having largest cross sectional area is:
questions.explanation: Capillaries have the largest total cross-sectional area.

questions.stem: Saliva is bactericidal because of presence of:
questions.explanation: Saliva is bactericidal because of lysozymes.

questions.stem: Percentage of CO2 carried by plasma?
questions.explanation: About 7% of CO2 is carried dissolved in plasma.

questions.stem: Valves are present in:
questions.explanation: Valves are present in abdominal veins.

questions.stem: Peptide bond is a:
questions.explanation: A peptide bond is a C-N link.

questions.stem: RNA retroviruses have special enzymes that:
questions.explanation: Retroviruses carry reverse transcriptase, which transcribes viral RNA to DNA.

questions.stem: Dub sound of heart is produced by:
questions.explanation: The dub sound comes from closure of the semilunar valves during ventricular relaxation.

questions.stem: Who gave this statement about the earth that it has 'No vestige of a beginning, no prospect of an end'?
questions.explanation: Hutton and Lyell stated the earth has no vestige of a beginning.

questions.stem: The SER is the major site of synthesis of:
questions.explanation: The SER is the major site of lipid synthesis.

questions.stem: CD receptors on T-Lymphocytes are in nature:
questions.explanation: CD receptors on T-lymphocytes are glycoproteins.

questions.stem: Fatigue free muscles are:
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle is fatigue-free.

questions.stem: Which of the following ions play important role in the transport of carbon dioxide?
questions.explanation: Chloride ions drive the chloride shift in CO2 transport.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is called milk sugar?
questions.explanation: Lactose is milk sugar.

questions.stem: Tailed bacteriophage is:
options: Motile on the surface of bacteria
Motile on the surface of plants
questions.explanation: Tailed bacteriophages are non-motile.

questions.stem: The temporary storage and ability to swim of sperm occurs in:
questions.explanation: Sperm are temporarily stored in the epididymis.

questions.stem: The brain contains:
questions.explanation: The brain contains glycolipids and cerebrosides.

questions.stem: A pea plant heterozygous for pod color is self-pollinated, which one of the following is true for green color
questions.explanation: Green pod colour is recessive, so 1/4 of the offspring are green.

questions.stem: Ribosomal RNA is actively synthesized in:
questions.explanation: rRNA is synthesized in the nucleolus.

questions.stem: In drosophila, a white eyed female will be produced by crossing:
options: White eyed male with red-eyed carrier female
White eyed male with red-eyed female
Red eyed male with red-eyed female
Red eyed male with red-eyed carrier female
questions.explanation: A white-eyed male crossed with a red-eyed carrier female can produce white-eyed females.

questions.stem: If medulla oblongata of a person brain is damaged, which of the following processes will be disturbed?
questions.explanation: The medulla controls swallowing, so its damage disturbs it.

questions.stem: Cells involved with protection, support and nourishment with the nervous system are called _______:
questions.explanation: Glial cells support and nourish neurons.

questions.stem: Vessel of the vessels is known as:
questions.explanation: The vessel of vessels is the vasa vasorum.

questions.stem: Lymph is returned to blood circulatory system in:
questions.explanation: Lymph returns to blood through the subclavian veins.

questions.stem: The second largest portion of human brain is:
questions.explanation: The cerebellum is the second largest part of the brain.

questions.stem: Trioses with keto group is:
questions.explanation: Dihydroxyacetone is a triose with a keto group.

questions.stem: Hybridoma cell is cultured in which medium?
questions.explanation: Hybridoma cells are cultured in HAT medium.

questions.stem: Example of fibrous proteins are all except:
questions.explanation: Albumin is a globular protein, not fibrous.

questions.stem: Of 100 ml of arterial blood, oxygen provided to the tissues is:
questions.explanation: About 5 ml of O2 per 100 ml blood is delivered to tissues.

questions.stem: Enzymes involved in cellular respiration are found in:
questions.explanation: Respiratory enzymes are found in the mitochondria.

questions.stem: Darwin observed how many different types of finches in Galapagos?
questions.explanation: Darwin observed 13 types of finches in Galapagos.

questions.stem: The amount of DNA in bacterial cell is:
questions.explanation: Bacterial DNA is about 3% of the cell.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is not true for skeletal muscles?
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle has many mitochondria, not one.

questions.stem: Normally each 100 ml blood contains ___ ml of O2 dissolved in plasma when PO2 is 95 mmHg:
questions.explanation: About 0.29 ml O2 is dissolved in 100 ml plasma at PO2 95 mmHg.

questions.stem: Main function of Golgi body is:
questions.explanation: The Golgi's main function is glycosylation.

questions.stem: Gonorrhea is a sex disease caused by:
questions.explanation: Gonorrhoea is caused by bacteria.

questions.stem: The strongest chamber in human heart is:
questions.explanation: The left ventricle is the strongest heart chamber.

questions.stem: True carbohydrates are:
questions.explanation: Monosaccharides are the true (simple) carbohydrates.

questions.stem: Enzymatic activities in saliva are increased by which one of the following ions?
questions.explanation: Chloride ions increase salivary enzyme activity.

questions.stem: Hamburger's phenomenon is also called:
questions.explanation: Hamburger's phenomenon is the chloride shift.

questions.stem: One of the following terms includes all others is:
questions.explanation: Metabolism includes oxidation, respiration and catabolism.

questions.stem: The joints where no movements occur relative to each other are called ______:
questions.explanation: Fixed (fibrous) joints allow no movement.

questions.stem: 2,4,6-trinitrophenol is commercially called as:
questions.explanation: 2,4,6-trinitrophenol is picric acid.

questions.stem: All of the following give positive response to Fehling reagent except:
questions.explanation: Benzaldehyde does not reduce Fehling's solution.

questions.stem: The rate of E1 reaction depends on:
questions.explanation: E1 rate depends on the concentration of the substrate.

questions.stem: How many oxygen atoms are present in 278 g of FeSO4.7H2O?
questions.explanation: 278 g FeSO4.7H2O is one mole containing 11 O atoms, i.e. 11 x NA.

questions.stem: Which is not used to calculate lattice energy of crystalline solids?
questions.explanation: The Haber process is not used to calculate lattice energy.

questions.stem: The general electronic configuration of d-block transition metals is (n-1)d1-10 ns1-2. The value of 'n' is:
questions.explanation: For d-block elements n ranges from 4 to 7.

questions.stem: Coinage metals are actually:
questions.explanation: Coinage metals are transition metals.

questions.stem: All of the following are basic except:
questions.explanation: BeO is amphoteric, not basic.

questions.stem: The carbonates of alkali metals are not affected by heat except:
questions.explanation: Li2CO3 decomposes on heating; other alkali carbonates are stable.

questions.stem: The unit of Boyle's constant K is:
questions.explanation: Boyle's constant K = PV, whose unit is the joule.

questions.stem: How many atoms are present in one BCC unit cell?
questions.explanation: A body-centred cubic unit cell contains 2 atoms.

questions.stem: Ice in water is in equilibrium, by increasing the pressure, equilibrium will shift:
questions.explanation: Higher pressure melts ice (volume decreases), shifting the equilibrium forward.

questions.stem: The isomer of a substance must have:
questions.explanation: Isomers must have the same molecular mass.

questions.stem: The formation of 1,3-butadiene always takes place through:
questions.explanation: 1,3-butadiene forms through sp2 hybridization.

questions.stem: The electrophile in aromatic sulphonation is:
questions.explanation: The electrophile in aromatic sulphonation is HSO3+.

questions.stem: Which of these processes involve weakening of the attraction between particles?
questions.explanation: Evaporation weakens attraction between particles.

questions.stem: Which one is the least reactive derivative of carboxylic acid?
questions.explanation: Amides are the least reactive carboxylic acid derivatives.

questions.stem: In a certain reaction the concentration is increased two times, and the rate is increased 8 times, the order
questions.explanation: Rate x8 with concentration x2 means order 3.

questions.stem: Which one is not endothermic?
questions.explanation: Condensation of vapours releases heat, so it is not endothermic.

questions.stem: The 1st ionization energy is higher for:
questions.explanation: Noble gases have the highest first ionisation energy.

questions.stem: The compound of Mn with zero reducing power is:
questions.explanation: KMnO4 is in its highest oxidation state and has no reducing power.

questions.stem: The sigma bond formed between carbon and oxygen atoms in aldehydes and ketones is due to overlap
questions.explanation: The C-O sigma bond in aldehydes/ketones is sp2-sp2.

questions.stem: Considering magnetic quantum number, which one is correct?
questions.explanation: The magnetic quantum number m ranges from -l to +l.

questions.stem: Which one has maximum number of unpaired electrons?
questions.explanation: Cr (atomic 24) has the maximum unpaired electrons.

questions.stem: For which mechanism, the 1st step involved is the same?
questions.explanation: E1 and SN1 both begin with formation of a carbocation.

questions.stem: Acidic hydrogen is present in:
questions.explanation: Acetylene (ethyne) has acidic hydrogen - both a and b.

questions.stem: Choose the aromatic one:
questions.explanation: Pyridine, thiophene and furan are all aromatic.

questions.stem: In nucleoproteins the prosthetic group is:
questions.explanation: Nucleoproteins have DNA or RNA as the prosthetic group.

questions.stem: What is the oxidizing agent in the following reaction? Zn + Cu2+ → Zn2+ + Cu
questions.explanation: Cu2+ is reduced, so it is the oxidizing agent.

questions.stem: Oxides and hydroxides of group IA are:
questions.explanation: Group IA oxides and hydroxides are strongly alkaline.

questions.stem: Phenol is more acidic than alcohol. Which statement is correct?
options: Phenol turns blue litmus paper red
Alcohol liberates CO2 with carbonate solution
Phenoxide ion is stabilized due to resonance
Alkoxide ion is stabilized due to resonance
questions.explanation: Phenol is more acidic because the phenoxide ion is resonance-stabilized.

questions.stem: Aldehydes are the oxidation product of:
questions.explanation: Aldehydes are the oxidation product of primary alcohols.

questions.stem: The fourth phase in the creation of a protein represents:
questions.explanation: The fourth phase of protein structure is quaternary, listed as 'None' here.

questions.stem: Benzene cannot undergo:
questions.explanation: Benzene cannot readily undergo addition reactions.

questions.stem: The complexes having coordination number = 4 have geometry:
options: May be tetrahedral or square planar
questions.explanation: Coordination number 4 gives tetrahedral or square planar geometry.

questions.stem: Magnetic moment of an atom or ion is the measure of its number of unpaired:
questions.explanation: Magnetic moment measures the number of unpaired electrons.

questions.stem: Shape of benzene molecule is:
questions.explanation: Benzene is a hexagonal planar molecule.

questions.stem: Which gas occupies the largest volume at STP?
questions.explanation: 4 g of H2 is 2 moles, the largest number of moles (largest volume).

questions.stem: In organic compounds carbon atoms form:
questions.explanation: Carbon atoms in organic compounds form covalent bonds.

questions.stem: Which are repelled by strong magnetic field?
questions.explanation: Diamagnetic substances are repelled by a strong magnetic field.

questions.stem: How many moles of product will be produced if one mole of CH4 is burnt completely?
questions.explanation: 1 mole CH4 gives 1 CO2 + 2 H2O = 3 moles of products.

questions.stem: Which one is not anisotropic behavior?
questions.explanation: Cleavage, conductivity and thermal expansion are all anisotropic; none is exempt.

questions.stem: In free fall motion normal force is:
questions.explanation: In free fall the normal force is zero.

questions.stem: When one mole of each of the following is completely burnt in oxygen, which will give the largest mass
questions.explanation: One mole of ethane gives the largest mass of CO2.

questions.stem: Which one has maximum number of moles?
questions.explanation: 48 g O2 = 1.5 mol, the most moles among the choices.

questions.stem: In free fall motion normal force is:
questions.explanation: In free fall the normal force is zero.

questions.stem: If the velocity of an object is 50i + 100j then how long will it remain in air? Take g = 10 m/s2:
questions.explanation: Time of flight = 2vy/g = 2 x 100/10 = 20 s.

questions.stem: The unit of grad V is _____:
questions.explanation: grad V is the electric field, whose unit is N/C.

questions.stem: Photoelectric effect was discovered by:
questions.explanation: Hertz discovered the photoelectric effect.

questions.stem: In photoelectric effect the number of electrons increases with increase in ______:
questions.explanation: The number of photoelectrons increases with light intensity.

questions.stem: The slope of charging of capacitor vs time graph is:
questions.explanation: The slope of the charging curve is q/C.

questions.stem: The ratio of weber and second gives:
questions.explanation: Weber/second is the volt.

questions.stem: A spring with spring constant k is cut into three equal pieces; if these pieces are connected in parallel
questions.explanation: Each piece has k' = 3k; three in parallel give 9k.
Weber/m2 is the tesla.

questions.stem: A soap bubble is given a charge then its radius is _______:
options: Change but information is insufficient that it may increase or decrease
questions.explanation: Charging a soap bubble makes its radius increase.

questions.stem: Two projectiles are fired from the same point with the same speed at angles of projection 60 and 30
options: Their maximum height will be same
Their vertical velocity will be same
Their time of flight will be same
questions.explanation: Projectiles at 60 and 30 have the same range.

questions.stem: Laminar flow is characterized by:
questions.explanation: Laminar flow occurs at low velocity.

questions.stem: A stone projected vertically upwards reaches a maximum height of h. When it is at a height 3h/4, the
questions.explanation: At 3h/4, PE:KE = 3:1, so KE:PE = 1:3.

questions.stem: The work done will be negative when the angle between force and displacement vectors is:
questions.explanation: Work is negative when 90 < theta <= 180.

questions.stem: A charged particle of mass m and charge q is released from rest in an electric field E, the velocity of
questions.explanation: v = Eqt/m for a particle in an electric field.

questions.stem: In hydrogen spectrum the infinite value of higher orbit (n = infinity) for all series corresponds to _______:
questions.explanation: The n = infinity limit is the series limit.

questions.stem: A radioactive sample decays 15/16 of original sample in 20 minutes, the half life of the sample is _____:
questions.explanation: Remaining 1/16 means 4 half-lives in 20 min, so 5 min each.

questions.stem: If the radius of the wire becomes half by stretching, then the new resistance will be (if initial resistance
questions.explanation: Radius halved (area /4, length x4) makes resistance 16R.

questions.stem: The unit of inductive reactance is?
questions.explanation: Inductive reactance is measured in ohms.

questions.stem: If the fundamental frequency f of a string fixed at both ends is 200 rps, the frequency of fifth harmonic
questions.explanation: The 5th harmonic = 5 x 200 = 1000 rps.

questions.stem: Which of the following allows current only in a single direction ______:
questions.explanation: A semi-conductor (diode) allows current in a single direction.

questions.stem: Cross product of vectors gives:
questions.explanation: Cross product gives rotation, area and a vector.

questions.stem: Which one is decreasing in charging of capacitor?
questions.explanation: The charging current I decreases over time.

questions.stem: An automobile travelling with speed of 60 km/hr is stopped in 20 m. If the car is going with speed 120
questions.explanation: Doubling speed quadruples stopping distance: 80 m.

questions.stem: A hollow metal sphere is charged to a potential V. The potential at its center is:
questions.explanation: The potential at the centre of a charged hollow sphere equals V.

questions.stem: For standing waves in a string whose both ends are closed, the number of nodes is ______ the number
questions.explanation: With both ends fixed, nodes exceed antinodes by one.

questions.stem: If a bomb dropped from an airplane explodes in mid-air:
questions.explanation: After mid-air explosion the kinetic energy increases.

questions.stem: Square root of (mu0 epsilon0) gives:
questions.explanation: sqrt(mu0 eps0) = 1/c = B/E.

questions.stem: The K.E of a charge particle changes when it passes through ______:
questions.explanation: Only an electric field changes a charged particle's kinetic energy.

questions.stem: By increasing pressure and temperature radioactivity _____:
questions.explanation: Radioactivity is unaffected by pressure and temperature.

questions.stem: The wind is blowing from south at 10 m/s but to a cyclist it appears to be blowing from east at 10 m/s,
questions.explanation: The cyclist moves at 10 sqrt(2) m/s towards the north-east.

questions.stem: Which statement is correct for a metallic conductor under electrostatic conditions?
options: E is zero inside the conductor
Potential is constant inside the conductor
E is perpendicular to the surface of the conductor
questions.explanation: E is zero inside, potential is constant, and E is normal to the surface.

questions.stem: If A represents ampere and R represents volt, then A/V, V/A and VA represent ______ respectively:
questions.explanation: A/V = conductance, V/A = resistance, VA = power.

questions.stem: At the top of the trajectory of a projectile, the directions of its velocity and acceleration are:
questions.explanation: At the top, velocity and acceleration are perpendicular.

questions.stem: A particle of mass m and charge q enters a magnetic field B perpendicularly with velocity v. The radius
questions.explanation: Radius r = mv/Bq.

questions.stem: Electromagnetic waves propagate along the X-axis and their electric field vibrates along the Y-axis, then
questions.explanation: The magnetic field vibrates along the Z-axis.

questions.stem: Which is a compound sentence?
options: He studied hard because he wanted to pass.
She was late, but she still finished the exam.
If it rains, we will cancel the trip.
Although he is old, he is very active.
questions.explanation: A compound sentence joins two clauses with 'but'.

questions.stem: Choose the correct sentence:
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is 'good at mathematics'.

questions.stem: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She sang yesterday beautifully at the concert.
She sang beautifully at the concert yesterday.
She sang at the concert yesterday beautifully.
She beautifully sang yesterday at the concert.
questions.explanation: Adverb of manner before place and time: sang beautifully at the concert yesterday.

questions.stem: I ___ to the market yesterday.
questions.explanation: The past tense 'went' fits the time marker 'yesterday'.

questions.stem: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: The adverb of frequency goes before the main verb.

questions.stem: They are watching a movie.
options: A movie is watched by them.
A movie is being watched by them.
A movie has been watched by them.
A movie was watched by them.
questions.explanation: Present continuous passive: 'A movie is being watched by them.'

questions.stem: Choose the simple sentence:
options: He reads books and she writes stories.
I opened the window to let in some fresh air.
Although he was sick, he went to school.
She cooked dinner while he cleaned the room.
questions.explanation: The only simple sentence has a single clause.

questions.stem: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: No comma is needed: 'Where are you going?'

questions.stem: She said, 'I am very tired today.'
options: She said that she is very tired today.
She said that she was very tired that day.
She says that she was very tired today.
She said that I was very tired that day. LOGICAL REASONING (9 MCQs)
questions.explanation: Reported speech shifts to past: 'she was very tired that day'.

questions.stem: What is the common ratio in the geometric progression 5, 15, 45, 135, ...?
questions.explanation: Each term is multiplied by 3, so the common ratio is 3.

questions.stem: Series: A, E, I, M, Q, ?
questions.explanation: Letters advance by 4: A, E, I, M, Q, U.

questions.stem: All athletes are fit. Some fit people are not disciplined. Conclusions: I. Some athletes are not disciplined.
questions.explanation: From the premises, only conclusion II follows.

questions.stem: Complete the series: 3, 4, 7, 11, 18, 29, 47, ?
questions.explanation: Differences follow Fibonacci: next term is 47 + 29 = 76.

questions.stem: Series: K, J, L, I, M, H, N, ?
questions.explanation: The pattern gives G then O after N.

questions.stem: What is the next term in the sequence: A, @, B, #, C, $, ______?
questions.explanation: Letters and symbols alternate: D, %.

questions.stem: Some mathematicians are philosophers. No philosopher is careless. Conclusions: I. Some
questions.explanation: Only conclusion I (some mathematicians are not careless) follows.

questions.stem: Complete the series: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 37, 50, ?
questions.explanation: Differences are odd numbers: next is 50 + 15 = 65.

questions.stem: Statement I: The government banned the use of plastic bags. Statement II: People shifted to cloth and
options: Statement I is the cause and Statement II is its effect.
Statement II is the cause and Statement I is its effect.
Both Statements I and II are independent causes.
Both Statements I and II are effects of independent causes.
questions.explanation: The ban (I) caused the shift to cloth bags (II).
